classification.difficultyReason: Explain subset properties using element membership, equality and finite cardinality.

content.prompt: Explain why each statement below is true.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $S$ is a set, then $\varnothing\subseteq S$.

answer.short: The empty set has no element outside $S$, so $\varnothing\subseteq S$.
answer.worked: A subset must have all its elements in $S$. The empty set has no elements, so it has no element outside $S$. Therefore $\varnothing\subseteq S$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $A\subseteq B$ and $B\subseteq C$, then $A\subseteq C$.

answer.short: Every element of $A$ belongs to $B$, and hence to $C$.
answer.worked: Every element of $A$ is in $B$. Every element of $B$ is in $C$, so every element of $A$ is also in $C$. Therefore $A\subseteq C$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If $S$ is a set, then $S\subseteq S$.

answer.worked: Every element of $S$ is an element of $S$ itself, which satisfies the definition of a subset. Therefore $S\subseteq S$.

answer.short: Each set contains every element of the other, so they have exactly the same elements.
answer.worked: Since $A\subseteq B$, every element of $A$ is in $B$. Since $B\subseteq A$, every element of $B$ is in $A$. Thus the sets have exactly the same elements, so $A=B$.

answer.short: The only element of $\{x\}$ is $x$, which belongs to $S$.
answer.worked: The set $\{x\}$ has only one element, $x$. Since $x\in S$, every element of $\{x\}$ is in $S$. Therefore $\{x\}\subseteq S$.

children.label: f
children.prompt: If $x\in S$ and $y\in S$, then $\{x,y\}\subseteq S$.

answer.worked: Each element of $\{x,y\}$ is either $x$ or $y$. Both belong to $S$, so every element of $\{x,y\}$ is in $S$. Therefore $\{x,y\}\subseteq S$.

children.label: g
children.prompt: If $A\subseteq B$, where $A$ and $B$ are finite sets, then $|A|\leq|B|$.

answer.short: $B$ contains every element of $A$, so it has at least as many elements as $A$.
answer.worked: Every element of $A$ belongs to $B$. Thus $B$ contains all the elements counted in $|A|$, and may contain more. Since the sets are finite, $|A|\leq|B|$.
